summary: Korbanos may come from grain grown in Eretz Yisrael or outside it, new or old, except the omer and the two loaves, which must be new grain from Eretz Yisrael. Everything is brought from the best grain, and the mishnah names the best places.

chunks.en: All the korbanos of the community and of a single person may come
chunks.st: All communal and individual meal offerings may come from

chunks.en: from Eretz Yisrael and from outside Eretz Yisrael,
chunks.st: produce grown in Eretz Yisrael and from outside Eretz Yisrael,

chunks.en: from the new grain and from the old.
chunks.st: from the new crop, i.e., the current year’s crop, and from the old crop from previous years.

chunks.en: Except the omer and the two loaves,
chunks.st: This is the halakha of all meal offerings except for the omer, i.e., the measure of barley brought as a communal offering on the sixteenth of Nisan, and the two loaves, i.e., the communal offering brought on the festival of Shavuot,

chunks.he: שֶׁאֵינָן בָּאִים אֶלָּא מִן הֶחָדָשׁ וּמִן הָאָרֶץ.
chunks.en: which come only from the new grain and from Eretz Yisrael.
chunks.st: as they come only from the new crop and from Eretz Yisrael.

chunks.he: וְכֻלָּן אֵינָן בָּאִים אֶלָּא מִן הַמֻּבְחָר.
chunks.en: And all of them come only from the best.
chunks.st: And all meal offerings come only from the optimal-quality grain.

chunks.en: And which is the best?
chunks.st: And which places have the optimal grain for them?

chunks.en: Michmas and Mezonicha
chunks.st: Fields in Makhnis and Zateḥa

chunks.en: are first for fine flour.
chunks.st: are the primary [alfa] source for fine flour.

words.note: Alfa, the first letter in Greek.

chunks.en: Second to them
chunks.st: Secondary to them is

chunks.en: is Chafarayim in the valley.
chunks.st: Aforayim in the valley.

chunks.en: All the lands were kosher,
chunks.st: All the regions were valid as the source of the grain,

chunks.en: but they would bring it from here.
chunks.st: but it is from here, the primary and secondary places, that they would bring grain, because it was of optimal quality.

summary: Grain for menachos should not come from a field that was fertilized, watered, or has trees, though after the fact it is kosher. The mishnah tells how to grow the best grain and how the treasurer checks the flour.
stIntro: Even when selecting grain for meal offerings from the locations mentioned in the previous mishna,

chunks.en: They do not bring grain from a fertilized field,
chunks.st: one may not bring as a meal offering grain from a fertilized field,

chunks.en: nor from a watered field,
chunks.st: nor from an irrigated field,

chunks.en: nor from a field of trees.
chunks.st: nor from a field of trees, as such fields do not produce grain of optimal quality.

chunks.en: But if he did bring it,
chunks.st: But if one did bring a meal offering of grain from such fields,

chunks.en: it is kosher. How does he do it?
chunks.st: it is fit. How does one produce optimal-quality grain?

chunks.en: He plows it the first year,
chunks.st: He plows the field during the first year, but he does not sow it,

chunks.he: וּבַשְּׁנִיָּה זוֹרְעָהּ קֹדֶם לַפֶּסַח שִׁבְעִים יוֹם,
chunks.en: and in the second year he plants it seventy days before Pesach,
chunks.st: and in the second year, he sows it seventy days before Passover, and

chunks.en: and it makes a lot of fine flour.
chunks.st: in that manner it produces grain that will provide an abundance of fine, high-quality, flour.

chunks.en: How does he check it?
chunks.st: How does the Temple treasurer inspect the flour to determine whether it is of sufficiently high quality?

chunks.en: The treasurer puts his hand into it.
chunks.st: The treasurer inserts his hand into the flour.

words.note: The person in charge of the Beis HaMikdash's money.

chunks.en: If dust came up on it,
chunks.st: If, when he removes his hand, flour powder covers it,

chunks.en: it is pasul until he sifts it.
chunks.st: the flour is unfit, until one sifts it with a fine sifter, so that no powder will remain.

chunks.en: And if it got wormy, it is pasul.
chunks.st: And if the flour became wormy, it is unfit for use in a meal offering.

summary: Tekoa had the best olive oil, and Regev was second. Oil from fertilized or watered groves is not first choice but is kosher. Oil from unripe olives, or olives soaked, pickled or cooked, is pasul.

chunks.en: Tekoa is first for oil.
chunks.st: Olive trees in Tekoa are the primary source of oil to be used in meal offerings.

chunks.en: Abba Shaul says:
chunks.st: Abba Shaul says:

chunks.en: Second to it is Regev, on the other side of the Yarden.
chunks.st: Secondary to Tekoa is Regev on the east bank of the Jordan River.

chunks.en: All the lands were kosher,
chunks.st: All the regions were valid for oil to be brought from them,

chunks.en: but they would bring it from here.
chunks.st: but it was from here that they would bring it.

chunks.en: They do not bring oil from a fertilized grove,
chunks.st: One may not bring a meal offering containing oil from olives taken from a fertilized olive grove,

chunks.en: nor from a watered grove,
chunks.st: nor from olives taken from an irrigated olive grove,

chunks.en: nor from what grain was planted between them.
chunks.st: nor from olives taken from an olive grove where grain was sown between the trees.

chunks.en: But if he did bring it,
chunks.st: But if one did bring a meal offering containing oil from such groves,

chunks.en: it is kosher. They do not bring oil from unripe olives.
chunks.st: it is valid. One may not bring a meal offering containing oil from unripe olives [anpiktan],

chunks.en: And if he did bring it,
chunks.st: but if one did bring it,

chunks.he: פָּסוּל. אֵין מְבִיאִין מִן הַגַּרְגְּרִים שֶׁנִּשְׁרוּ בַמַּיִם,
chunks.en: it is pasul. They do not bring from olives soaked in water,
chunks.st: it is not valid. One may not bring a meal offering containing oil from olives that were soaked in water,

chunks.en: nor from pickled ones,
chunks.st: nor from pickled olives,

chunks.en: nor from cooked ones.
chunks.st: nor from boiled olives,

chunks.en: And if he did bring it, it is pasul.
chunks.st: and even if one did bring it, it is not valid.

summary: Olives ripen in three rounds, and from each round three kinds of oil are made. The first oil drips out by itself after crushing; more is pressed out with a beam (or stones, says Rabbi Yehuda); the last comes after grinding. The very first oil goes to the Menorah, and the rest to menachos.

chunks.en: There are three olive harvests,
chunks.st: There are three harvests of olives each year,

words.note: Three harvests of olives each year.

chunks.en: and in them, three kinds of oil each.
chunks.st: and in each of them, three different grades of oils are produced.

chunks.en: The first olive harvest:
chunks.st: How is the first olive harvest processed?

chunks.en: He picks it at the top of the olive tree, and crushes it,
chunks.st: One picks the ripe olives at the top of the olive tree, as those are the first to ripen, and crushes them in a mortar

chunks.en: and puts it into the basket.
chunks.st: and places them inside the bottom of a wicker basket that has many small holes in it.
chunks.stMore: The oil will then drip from the olives through those holes into a vessel placed underneath the basket.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: Around the sides of the basket.
chunks.st: One positions the olives on the walls, surrounding the basket. This produces more refined oil, as the dregs stick to the walls of the basket.

chunks.en: This is the first oil.
chunks.st: This is the first grade of oil produced from the first harvest.

chunks.en: He presses it with a beam.
chunks.st: After the oil ceases to seep from the crushed olives, one then presses down with a wooden beam upon them, causing additional oil to flow from the basket into the vessel.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:
chunks.stMore: The excessive pressure produced by pressing down with a beam would cause some of the flesh of the olives to get mixed in with the oil, compromising its quality.

chunks.en: With stones. This is the second oil.
chunks.st: Rather, one applies pressure by placing stones upon the olives. This is the second grade of oil.

chunks.en: He went back and ground it and pressed it;
chunks.st: One then ground the olives with a millstone and pressed down with a beam on those olives to extract any remaining oil;

chunks.en: this is the third oil.
chunks.st: this is the third grade of oil.

chunks.en: The first oil is for the Menorah,
chunks.st: The first grade is fit for kindling the Candelabrum, which requires: “Refined olive oil” (Leviticus 24:2),

chunks.en: and the rest is for the menachos.
chunks.st: and the rest are fit for use in meal offerings.

chunks.en: The second olive harvest: he picks it at roof height,
chunks.st: How is the second olive harvest processed? One picks the crop of olives that is accessible while one is standing on the rooftop. This was the second lot of olives to ripen.

chunks.en: and crushes it and puts it into the basket.
chunks.st: And one crushes it in a mortar and places those olives into a wicker basket, allowing the oil to drip through the holes into a vessel underneath.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: Around the sides of the basket.
chunks.st: One positions the olives on the walls, surrounding the basket.

chunks.en: This is the first oil.
chunks.st: This is the first grade of oil from the second harvest.

chunks.en: He presses it with a beam.
chunks.st: One then presses down upon those olives with a wooden beam, thereby producing more oil.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says:
chunks.st: And Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: With stones. This is the second oil.
chunks.st: One applies pressure only by placing stones upon them. This is the second grade of oil.

chunks.en: He went back and ground it and pressed it;
chunks.st: One then ground the olives with a millstone and pressed down upon them with a beam, thereby extracting any remaining oil;

chunks.en: this is the third oil.
chunks.st: this is the third grade of oil.

chunks.en: The first oil is for the Menorah,
chunks.st: The first grade is fit for kindling the Candelabrum,

chunks.en: and the rest is for the menachos.
chunks.st: and the rest are fit for use in meal offerings.

chunks.en: The third olive harvest:
chunks.st: How is the third olive harvest processed?
chunks.stMore: This harvest consists of all the olives that still remain on trees.

chunks.en: He packs it inside the building until it gets soft,
chunks.st: One packs it into a vat [oteno] in the building that houses the olive press [beit habbad] where it remains until it softens,

chunks.en: and brings it up and dries it on the roof,
chunks.st: and then one raises it up to the roof and dries it on the rooftop to remove the foul-smelling liquid secreted from the olives while in the vat.

chunks.en: and crushes it and puts it into the basket.
chunks.st: Then, one crushes the olives in a mortar and places them into a wicker basket, allowing the oil to drip through the holes into a vessel underneath.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: Around the sides of the basket.
chunks.st: One positions them on the walls, surrounding the basket.

chunks.en: This is the first oil.
chunks.st: This is the first grade of oil.

chunks.en: He presses it with a beam.
chunks.st: One then presses down on those olives with a wooden beam, thereby producing more oil.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says:
chunks.st: And Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: With stones. This is the second oil.
chunks.st: One applies pressure only by placing stones upon them. This is the second grade of oil.

chunks.en: He went back and ground it and pressed it;
chunks.st: One would then grind the olives with a millstone and press down upon them with a beam, thereby extracting any remaining oil;

chunks.en: this is the third oil.
chunks.st: this is the third grade of oil.

chunks.en: The first oil is for the Menorah,
chunks.st: The first grade is fit for kindling the Candelabrum,

chunks.en: and the rest is for the menachos.
chunks.st: and the rest are fit for use in meal offerings.

summary: The mishnah ranks the nine kinds of oil from best to worst. One might think menachos need the best oil like the Menorah, but the pasuk says the pure, crushed oil is only needed "for light."
stIntro: Having enumerated the nine grades of oils in the previous mishna, this mishna proceeds to rank them by their quality:

chunks.en: The first oil of the first harvest:
chunks.st: As for the first grade of oil that is produced from the first harvest,

chunks.en: there is none better than it.
chunks.st: there is none superior to it.

chunks.en: The second of the first and the first of the second
chunks.st: The second grade of oil that is produced from the first harvest and the first grade of oil that is produced from the second harvest

chunks.he: שָׁוִין. הַשְּׁלִישִׁי שֶׁבָּרִאשׁוֹן וְהַשֵּׁנִי שֶׁבַּשֵּׁנִי וְהָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁבַּשְּׁלִישִׁי,
chunks.en: are equal. The third of the first, the second of the second, and the first of the third
chunks.st: are of equal quality; there is no reason to choose one over the other. The third grade of oil that is produced from the first harvest and the second grade of oil that is produced from the second harvest and the first grade of oil that is produced from the third harvest

chunks.en: are equal. The third of the second and the second of the third
chunks.st: are of equal quality. The third grade of oil that is produced from the second harvest and the second grade of oil that is produced from the third harvest

chunks.en: are equal. The third of the third:
chunks.st: are of equal quality. As for the third grade of oil that is produced from the third harvest,

chunks.en: there is none worse than it.
chunks.st: there is none inferior to it.

chunks.en: It would make sense that the menachos also
chunks.st: Also, with regard to all the meal offerings, it was logical

chunks.en: should need pure olive oil.
chunks.st: that they should require the highest quality of refined olive oil, just like the Candelabrum.

chunks.en: If the Menorah, which is not for eating,
chunks.st: Because if the Candelabrum, whose oil is not to be consumed on the altar,

chunks.en: needs pure olive oil,
chunks.st: requires refined olive oil,

chunks.en: then the menachos, which are for eating,
chunks.st: then meal offerings, which are to be consumed on the altar,

chunks.he: אֵינוֹ דִין שֶׁיִּטָּעֲנוּ שֶׁמֶן זַיִת זַךְ.
chunks.en: shouldn't they surely need pure olive oil?
chunks.st: is it not logical that they should require refined olive oil?

chunks.en: The pasuk teaches (Shemos 27):
chunks.st: To dispel this notion, the verse states: “

chunks.en: "Pure and crushed for light,"
chunks.st: Refined pounded olive oil for illumination”
chunks.stMore: (Leviticus 24:2), which indicates that the high-quality, refined, pounded oil is required for the Candelabrum,

chunks.en: but pure and crushed is not needed for the menachos.
chunks.st: but there is no need for refined pounded olive oil for meal offerings.

summary: The best wine for nesachim came from Keruchim and Atulim, and second best from Beis Rimah, Beis Lavan and Kfar Signah. Some wines are not first choice but kosher; sweet, smoked or cooked wine is pasul. Wine should come from grapes near the ground in a well-tended vineyard.

chunks.en: From where would they bring the wine?
chunks.st: From where would they bring the wine for libations?

chunks.en: Keruchim and Atulim
chunks.st: Keduḥim and Attulin

chunks.en: are first for wine.
chunks.st: are the primary sources for wine.

chunks.en: Second to them
chunks.st: Secondary to them is

chunks.en: are Beis Rimah and Beis Lavan in the mountains,
chunks.st: Beit Rima and Beit Lavan, located in the mountain, and

chunks.en: and Kfar Signah in the valley.
chunks.st: the village of Signa, located in the valley.

chunks.en: All the lands were kosher,
chunks.st: All the regions were valid sources for wine;

chunks.en: but they would bring it from here.
chunks.st: but it was from here, i.e., the aforementioned locations, that they would bring the wine.

chunks.en: They do not bring wine
chunks.st: One may not bring libations of wine that come

chunks.en: from a fertilized vineyard,
chunks.st: from a fertilized vineyard,

chunks.en: nor from a watered vineyard,
chunks.st: or from an irrigated vineyard,

chunks.en: nor from what grain was planted between the vines.
chunks.st: or from a vineyard in which grain was sown between the vines.

chunks.en: But if he did bring it,
chunks.st: But if one did bring a libation from such wine,

chunks.en: it is kosher. They do not bring wine made from sun-dried grapes.
chunks.st: it is valid. One may not bring libations from sweet wine made from sun-dried grapes [hilyasteyon],

chunks.en: And if he did bring it,
chunks.st: but if one did bring a libation from such wine,

chunks.en: it is kosher. They do not bring old wine,
chunks.st: it is valid. One may not bring wine aged for one year;

chunks.en: says Rebbi.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi,

chunks.en: But the Sages say it is kosher.
chunks.st: but the Rabbis deem it valid.

chunks.en: They do not bring wine
chunks.st: One may not bring libations from

chunks.en: that is sweet,
chunks.st: sweet wine,

chunks.en: nor smoked,
chunks.st: nor from wine produced from smoked grapes,

chunks.en: nor cooked.
chunks.st: nor libations from boiled wine,

chunks.en: And if he did bring it,
chunks.st: and if one did bring a libation from such wine,

chunks.en: it is pasul. They do not bring wine from grapes hanging high on trees,
chunks.st: it is not valid. And one may not bring wine produced from grapes suspended on stakes or trees;

chunks.he: אֶלָּא מִן הָרוֹגְלִיּוֹת וּמִן הַכְּרָמִים הָעֲבוּדִים:
chunks.en: but from grapes near the ground and from well-tended vineyards.
chunks.st: rather, one brings it from grapes at foot height, i.e., that rest on the ground, which are superior-quality grapes, and from vineyards that are cultivated, i.e., where one hoes beneath the vines twice a year.

words.note: Grapes near the ground, which are better.

summary: Wine for nesachim was stored in small jugs, not too full, so it would keep its smell. They took wine from the middle of the jug, not the top or the bottom. The treasurer watched the wine flow and signaled to stop it when the scum started to come.

chunks.he: לֹא הָיוּ כוֹנְסִים אוֹתוֹ בַחֲצָבִים גְּדוֹלִים,
chunks.en: They would not store the wine in big barrels,
chunks.st: And when producing wine for libations, one should not collect the wine into large barrels, as it causes the wine to spoil;

chunks.en: but in small jugs.
chunks.st: rather, it should be placed in small casks.

chunks.he: וְאֵינוֹ מְמַלֵּא אֶת הֶחָבִיּוֹת עַד פִּיהֶם,
chunks.en: And he does not fill the jugs up to the top,
chunks.st: And one does not fill up the cask until its mouth; rather,

chunks.en: so that its smell will spread.
chunks.st: one leaves some empty space so that its fragrance will collect there and diffuse when the lid is opened.

chunks.en: He does not bring wine
chunks.st: One should not bring libations

chunks.en: from the top of the jug,
chunks.st: from wine that rests at the mouth of the cask

chunks.en: because of the white scum,
chunks.st: due to the flour-like white scum that floats on the surface,

words.note: A thin white layer that floats on top of wine.

chunks.en: nor from its bottom,
chunks.st: nor from the wine at bottom of the cask

chunks.en: because of the dregs.
chunks.st: due to the sediment that collects there.

words.note: What sinks to the bottom of the jug.

chunks.en: Rather, he brings it from its middle third.
chunks.st: Rather, one brings from the wine in its middle third.

chunks.en: How does he check?
chunks.st: How does the Temple treasurer inspect the wine to determine that it is from the middle of the cask?

chunks.en: The treasurer sits with the reed in his hand.
chunks.st: The treasurer sits alongside the cask and has the measuring reed in his hand.

chunks.en: When the scum came out, he knocked with the reed.
chunks.st: The spigot is opened and the wine begins to flow. When he sees that the wine emerging draws with it chalk-like scum [hagir], he immediately knocks with the reed to indicate that the spigot should be closed.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, says:

chunks.en: Wine that has white scum in it
chunks.st: Wine in which there is flour-like white scum is

chunks.en: is pasul, as it says:
chunks.st: unfit for libations, as it is stated with regard to animal offerings:

chunks.en: "They shall be perfect for you, and their mincha" (Bamidbar 28),
chunks.st: “Unblemished they shall be for you…and their meal offering shall be fine flour mixed with oil…

chunks.en: "they shall be perfect for you, and their nesachim."
chunks.st: unblemished they shall be for you, and their libations” (Numbers 28:19–20, 31).
chunks.stMore: This indicates that animal offerings, meal offerings, and libations must all be brought from flawless products. Therefore, the presence of flour-like white scum in wine renders it unfit.
